Class Index

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.Index
@Internal public final class Index extends Object
The reader of MICRONAUT-INF/index.bin, the table of contents a runner jar carries so that the launcher never parses a nested archive at startup.

The index is used in place: the bytes stay in the memory mapping and every accessor is a bounds-checked read at a computed offset. Records are addressed by plain int indexes, never by objects, because materialising one object per entry would cost more than everything else the launcher does; a Micronaut application indexes on the order of fifteen thousand entries.

Validation

Opening the index checks everything that can be checked in constant time or in time proportional to the (small) jar table: magic, format version, section bounds, a power of two hash table, a sane probe limit, and that the recorded outer file length still matches the file. Anything that would cost time proportional to the entry table, such as verifying every string reference, is checked when the record is touched instead, so that opening the index faults in only the pages it needs. Failures throw IllegalStateException with a message that asks for the jar to be rebuilt, because in practice they all mean the same thing: the jar was edited, truncated or rebuilt after it was packaged.

Thread safety

Accessors use absolute ByteBuffer reads, which do not touch the buffer position, so an instance is safe for concurrent use by any number of class-loading threads. Package-name lookups lazily publish immutable, bounded per-jar hash tables through atomic references. validateJar(int) writes a boolean into an array; the write is idempotent, so a race only means the check runs twice.

The class is public because runner-build writes and checks archives with it, and io.micronaut.runner.protocol.jar and the benchmarks read them; it is not API for applications.

Since:
1.0

    • validateJar

      public void validateJar(int jarId)
      Checks, once per jar, that the nested jar still starts where the index says it does.

      This is the second half of the staleness check: the file length caught a rebuild that changed the size, and the local file header signature can catch one that did not but moved this jar. It costs a single four byte read the first time a jar is touched, and a successful result is cached. The application layer is not a nested jar and is never checked.

      A header offset outside the archive means the index does not describe this file, so it is reported as a stale jar. A read that fails for any other reason, for example because the source was closed, says nothing about the jar and is reported as the I/O failure it is.

      Parameters:
      jarId - the jar index
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the archive no longer agrees with the index
      UncheckedIOException - if the local file header cannot be read

    • openEntryStream

      public InputStream openEntryStream(int record) throws IOException
      Opens one indexed entry after performing its jar's lazy staleness check. Every stream of an entry, whether for the class loader, a NestedJarFile view or a jar: URL, is opened here.

      When micronaut.runner.verify was "true" as this index was opened, every byte returned or skipped contributes to the CRC-32, and the checksum is compared as soon as the recorded end of the entry is reached. Closing a partially read stream does not drain or verify it.

      Parameters:
      record - the entry record
      Returns:
      a fresh stream over the entry
      Throws:
      IOException - if the entry cannot be opened or fails verification

    • find

      public int find(String logicalName)
      Looks up a logical name and returns the head of its chain.

      The chain holds every record with that name across all jars, in classpath order, with a jar's versioned aliases before its base record; the launcher picks the record that applies, and resolveInJar(int, int, int) picks the one of a given jar. The candidate's name is compared against the stored UTF-8 bytes without allocating: the lengths are compared first, then the bytes, and only a name that actually contains a non-ASCII character is decoded.

      Parameters:
      logicalName - the entry name relative to its jar, with no leading slash
      Returns:
      the first record with that name, or IndexFormat.NO_INDEX

    • findClass

      public int findClass(String binaryName)
      Looks up the resource that holds a class and returns the head of its chain.

      This is the most executed method in the launcher: every class the application loads comes through it. It never builds the resource name. The hash of binaryName.replace('.', '/') + ".class" is computed straight from the binary name, using the identity hashCode(a + b) == hashCode(a) * 31^length(b) + hashCode(b) to fold in the suffix, and the candidate is verified by comparing the stored UTF-8 bytes while mapping dots to slashes on the fly. No allocation happens on the hit path, the miss path or the collision path.

      Parameters:
      binaryName - the class name, for example org.example.Service$Inner
      Returns:
      the first record for that class, or IndexFormat.NO_INDEX

    • validateStringReferences

      public void validateStringReferences()
      Walks every string reference in the index and checks that it lies inside the string table.

      open(ArchiveSource) deliberately does not do this: it is the one validation whose cost grows with the number of entries, and it would fault in the whole entry and string tables before the application starts. References are bounds-checked when they are dereferenced instead. Tools that dump an index, and tests, call this to check the whole file up front.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if any reference points outside the string table
